body:
`case_study:enron-2001` | 2001-12-02 | tickers: US-ENRNQ | confidence: verified

Enron peaked at ~$90 in Aug 2000 (market cap ~$70 bn) and filed for bankruptcy on 2 Dec 2001 with the stock under $1. Mechanics: mark-to-market accounting booked the estimated lifetime profit of long-dated energy contracts upfront; off-balance-sheet special-purpose entities (Chewco, LJM, Raptors) run by CFO Andrew Fastow hid debt and hedged Enron's own stock; restatement of 1997-2001 earnings in Nov 2001; auditor Arthur Andersen shredded documents and collapsed. Visible flags: (1) reported earnings far above operating cash flow (much 'cash flow' came from asset sales and prepay deals); (2) low return on capital (~single digit) despite 'asset-light' trading claims; (3) opaque segment disclosure -- Bethany McLean's Fortune article 'Is Enron Overpriced?' (5 Mar 2001) asked simply how Enron made money; (4) Jim Chanos (Kynikos) shorted from late 2000 on poor ROIC vs cost of capital, related-party SPEs and insider selling; (5) executives sold large blocks of stock in 2000-01; (6) CEO Skilling resigned abruptly in Aug 2001 after six months; (7) Cornell MBA students flagged Enron with the Beneish M-score in 1998. Lesson: when you can't explain how a company earns cash, assume it doesn't; related-party entities run by the CFO and CEO departures 'for personal reasons' are disqualifiers.

**Lesson:** Explain the cash or walk away
**Spotted early by:** Jim Chanos; Bethany McLean (Fortune); Cornell students
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:forensic-redflag-checklist`, illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`, illustrates -> `insight:beneish-m-score`
**Sources:** <https://fortune.com/2015/12/30/is-enron-overpriced-fortune-2001/> ; <https://www.sechistorical.org/museum/galleries/wwr/wwr06a-scandals-enron.php> ; <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beneish_M-score>

**NO-GO.** No pre-registered test meets its go bar. The 12-month excess return is measured against
sector-and-size-matched controls; "wins." means the 5/95% winsorised mean.

| Test (12 m) | n | Mean [95% firm-bootstrap CI] | Wins. mean | Median | Hit | t | Go bar | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **H1** MD&A Jaccard, bottom quintile (big change) | 60 | −2.1% [−16.4, +14.7] | −4.1% | −16.8% | 37% | −0.30 | wins. ≤ −5%, median < 0, t ≤ −1.5 | **fail** (wins. and t miss the bar) |
| **H2** Auditor + CARO Jaccard, bottom quintile | 65 | −0.8% [−13.0, +11.9] | −3.7% | −10.0% | 42% | −0.12 | same | **fail** |
| **H3** new auditor-section adverse item (hand-checked) | 21 | **+7.7%** [−15.2, +34.4] | +4.8% | **+17.5%** | 52% | +0.60 | ≥ 10 flags, wins. ≤ −10%, median < 0 | **fail** (wrong sign) |
| Feasibility: share of attempted pairs usable | MD&A 298/385 = **77%**; auditor 319/385 = **83%** | | | | | | ≥ 75% | pass |

Calibration (descriptive): all scored events vs controls were −4.0% (MD&A sample, t −1.35) and −6.6% (auditor
sample, t −2.41, CI −12.2 to −1.1). The 200 text firms lagged the 150 control-only firms over these two years,
which is sampling noise in a small pool where single stocks move ±100%. **Relative to the other text firms**,
the big changers did *better*, not worse: MD&A Q1 was +1.9 pp vs all events, auditor Q1 +5.8 pp. So the
negative raw numbers in H1 and H2 are not a text-change effect.

**Reading.** The fee replaced a margin that MHVSIL used to earn on resale (Q1 FY26 call: MHVSIL's gross margin on that business was "typically
10%"; an analyst calculated it implied 40–50% gross margin on its remaining aftermarket business — management "has not reviewed their financials").
OPM after the switch went *up* 0.3 pt, so the switch did not leak value on the evidence we have. But the fee is (a) **renewed annually** (next
30-Apr-2027), (b) ₹97.5 cr sits below the material-RPT approval threshold (lower of ₹1,000 cr or 10% of last audited turnover ≈ ₹208–218 cr), so shareholders do not vote on it, and
(c) its pricing formula is not disclosed ("arm's length"). **Dated watch items:** services agreement expiry 30-Apr-2027; FY27 AR note 29 fee line;
any new MRPT resolution. Also: the CCI order on Bharat Forge (commitments on access to AAL's business information) `[AR26 secretarial audit]`.

**Inputs collected (L8 step 1):** close ₹1,776.30 on 23-Nov-2026 (NSE bhavcopy = Yahoo); 10 FY-end P/Es FY17–26 (21.6, 26.1, 16.0, 14.1, 70.3, 34.8,
22.1, 16.0, 15.7, 14.2; median 18.8 — cyclical: high at troughs); peers GNA 15.6 / JAMNAAUTO 20.8 / WHEELS 29.7; 6-month ADV ₹2.44 cr mean, ₹1.05 cr
median `[YH]`; net cash ₹393.9 cr; no pending dilution.
**Scenarios (written before the outputs; cycle position in FY31–32):** bear 35% (revenue ~flat over 5 years, NOPAT margin → 5.5%, ROIIC 15%, exit 14x);
base 45% (+5–6%/yr, 6.8%, 18%, 16x); bull 17% (+11% fading to 7%, 8.0%, 22%, 18x); blow-up 3% (0.3x: Customer A dual-sources in a downturn + fee step-up).
**Outputs:** 5-year multiples bear 1.04x / base 1.60x / bull 2.32x; **EV 1.49x raw, 1.40x anchored** vs hurdle 1.76x; P(≥2x) 24%, P(≥3x) 6%, P(≤0.5x) 4%
raw (8.2% anchored), P(blow-up) 3% raw (10.4% anchored). Base-case IRR **10.4%** vs CoE 12.5%. Probability-weighted DCF ₹1,316 (−26%).
**Exit-multiple bet:** DCF-consistent exit P/E 11.5–12.2 vs used 14/16/18 vs own median 18.8 → EV 1.13x / 1.49x / 1.73x. Even at the own-median exit the
EV (1.73x) sits just under the hurdle: **the binding choice is again the exit multiple** (L36), and for a cyclical the right exit multiple depends
on where FY31 sits in the cycle.
**Temperature:** trailing 12.9x = **COLD** (0th percentile of own history, 0.62x sector median); on 10-year normalised EPS ₹68.9 = 25.8x = **WARM**
(70th percentile). Reverse DCF at flat 7.7% NOPAT margin needs 12.6% revenue CAGR for 10 years — far above the 4.4% peak-to-peak EPS CAGR.
